newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea seen losing supervisory role-reports.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea seen losing supervisory role-reports.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea is likely to lose its bank supervisory functions under the final government draft of financial reforms, local media reported on Sunday.
Instead, the central bank will be given the rights to ask the proposed unified financial watchdog to inspect banks and to jointly examine banks, they said.
President Kim Young-sam on Saturday approved the final government draft of financial reforms submitted by the finance minister.

The final draft will be revealed on Monday in a joint news conference by the Minister of Finance and Economy Kang Kyong-shik, the central Bank of Korea governor Lee Kyung-shick and the head of the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform Park Seong-yawng.
The final draft proposed that the banking, insurance and securities supervisory bodies should be unified under the authority of the prime minister.
This was one of the suggestions provided by the presidential commission studying financial reforms earlier this month.
The commission also proposed granting more autonomy to financial institutions, increasing Central Bank independence and lifting various government regulations.

The media also reported that the final government package left out a controversial issue over a rise of the bank ownership limit. The commission has proposed raising the ceiling to 10 percent from the current four percent under certain conditions and with prior government approval.
The finance ministry is expected to submit the draft to a special parliamentary session of the National Assembly in the near future.
